## README.md
# LANDFIRE 2024 Update (LF 2024, version 2.5.0) — CONUS, 30 m

[LANDFIRE](https://landfire.gov) is a shared program of the U.S. Geological Survey and the USDA
Forest Service that maps vegetation, fuel and fire-regime conditions across the United States at
30 m resolution. This bucket holds the **LANDFIRE 2024 Update (version 2.5.0)** for the
conterminous United States.

License: **public domain** (a work of the U.S. federal government).
Source: <https://landfire.gov/data/FullExtentDownloads>, accessed **2026-08-25**.

**LANDFIRE 2024 is the most recent release that carries Vegetation Condition Class** — the 2025
release (2.6.0) ships EVC, EVT and FBFM40 but not VCC, SClass or VDep.

> ⚠️ **Vintage.** Wildfire Hazard Potential 2023, published elsewhere in this catalog, is built
> from LANDFIRE **2020 (2.2.0)** fuels — three updates older than the data here. The two are not
> the same vintage; do not combine them as though they were.

## Collections

| Collection | Layer | Codes in CONUS | Status |
|---|---|---|---|
| `landfire-2024-vcc` | Vegetation Condition Class — departure from reference condition | 11 | **published** |
| `landfire-2024-evt` | Existing Vegetation Type | 830 | **published** |
| `landfire-2024-evc` | Existing Vegetation Cover | 265 | not yet published |
| `landfire-2024-fbfm40` | 40 Scott & Burgan fire behavior fuel models | 44 | not yet published |

> **What is not here yet.** Only the dominant-class (`hex`) tables are published, for VCC and EVT.
> The per-class fractional-coverage (`hex-fractions`) tables — the ones area accounting needs — are
> not published for any layer, and EVC and FBFM40 are not published at all. Use cell counts from
> the `hex` tables for distributions, and treat any area figure derived from them as approximate:
> each cell contributes its dominant class only.

Each published collection has these assets:

| Asset | Format | Path |
|---|---|---|
| `<layer>-cog` | Cloud-Optimized GeoTIFF (EPSG:4326, Int16) | `…/landfire-2024-<layer>/landfire-2024-<layer>-cog.tif` |
| `<layer>-hex` | H3 hex parquet, resolution 10, **dominant class** | `…/landfire-2024-<layer>/hex/h0=*/data_0.parquet` |

Base URL: `https://s3-west.nrp-nautilus.io/public-landfire/`

H3 native resolution **10** (~15,000 m², roughly 16 source pixels per cell), with parents
**9, 8, 0**. `h8` is the catalog's universal join key; `h0` is the hive partition key.

## Which hex table to use

`hex` keeps only the class covering the largest share of each cell, so the mix inside a cell is
lost. It answers "what is this place mostly".

`hex-fractions` is long format — one row per (cell, class), with `frac` giving that class's share
of the cell. **It is the table for any question about how much area a class holds.** Fractions
within a cell sum to 1 or less; the shortfall is the part of the cell with no valid source pixel.

```sql
INSTALL httpfs; LOAD httpfs;
-- Share of CONUS in each Vegetation Condition Class, area-weighted
SELECT vcc, SUM(frac) / SUM(SUM(frac)) OVER () AS share
FROM read_parquet('https://s3-west.nrp-nautilus.io/public-landfire/landfire-2024-vcc/hex-fractions/h0=*/data_0.parquet')
WHERE vcc BETWEEN 1 AND 6          -- exclude water, snow, developed, barren, agriculture
GROUP BY vcc ORDER BY vcc;
```

For ground area rather than a share, weight `frac` by each cell's area — see the catalog h3-guide
for the area method rather than a nominal per-resolution constant.

## Codes that are not a condition

Every layer carries codes for land that is not rated. Exclude them from the denominator of any
"share of land that is X" statistic:

| Layer | Codes to exclude |
|---|---|
| VCC | `111` water, `112` snow/ice, `120` developed, `132` barren/sparse, `180` agriculture |
| EVC | `11`–`32` water/snow/developed/barren/quarries, `61`–`82` agriculture, `100` sparse |
| FBFM40 | `91`, `92`, `93`, `98`, `99` — the non-burnable models NB1, NB2, NB3, NB8, NB9 |
| EVT | roll up with `EVT_LF` / `EVT_PHYS` in the shipped legend |

**Fill codes are already excluded from the hex tables.** Every layer carries `-9999` and `32767`
as fill, and VCC additionally carries `-1111`. These were measured from the full source rasters,
not read from the product metadata, which understates them. They survive as pixel values in the
COGs (where `-9999` is the declared NoData) and are documented in each COG's
`classification:classes`.

## Reading EVC — the codes are not percentages

EVC combines lifeform with percent cover in a single code:

| Value range | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `11`–`32` | water, snow/ice, developed, barren, quarries |
| `61`–`82` | agriculture |
| `100` | sparse vegetation — carries no percentage |
| `110`–`199` | **tree** cover = value − 100 % |
| `210`–`299` | **shrub** cover = value − 200 % |
| `310`–`399` | **herb** cover = value − 300 % |

```sql
-- correct: decode, then average within one lifeform
SELECT AVG(evc - 100) AS mean_tree_cover_pct
FROM read_parquet('https://s3-west.nrp-nautilus.io/public-landfire/landfire-2024-evc/hex/h0=*/data_0.parquet')
WHERE evc BETWEEN 110 AND 199;
-- wrong: AVG(evc) averages across lifeforms — the mean of a 15% tree code (115) and a
-- 15% shrub code (215) is 165, which decodes as "tree cover 65%"
```

## Displaying a COG (MapLibre GL JS via TiTiler)

These are rasters — there is no PMTiles layer and no vector `source-layer`. Render the COG through
a TiTiler XYZ endpoint, using the published class palette (`classification:classes` in the STAC
gives every code an RGB `color_hint`):

```js
map.addSource('landfire-vcc', {
  type: 'raster',
  tiles: ['https://titiler.../cog/tiles/{z}/{x}/{y}.png?url=' +
    encodeURIComponent('https://s3-west.nrp-nautilus.io/public-landfire/landfire-2024-vcc/landfire-2024-vcc-cog.tif') +
    '&colormap=' + encodeURIComponent(JSON.stringify(vccColormap))],   // from classification:classes
  tileSize: 256
});
map.addLayer({ id: 'landfire-vcc', type: 'raster', source: 'landfire-vcc' });
```

## Vegetation Condition Class codes

| Code | Class | Departure |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | Condition Class I.A | Very low — 0–16% |
| 2 | Condition Class I.B | Low — 17–33% |
| 3 | Condition Class II.A | Moderate to low — 34–50% |
| 4 | Condition Class II.B | Moderate to high — 51–66% |
| 5 | Condition Class III.A | High — 67–83% |
| 6 | Condition Class III.B | Very high — 84–100% |
| 111 | Water | not rated |
| 112 | Snow / ice | not rated |
| 120 | Developed | not rated |
| 132 | Barren or sparsely vegetated | not rated |
| 180 | Agriculture | not rated |
